## Turn 34: Assistant

### Root Cause Analysis

The error **`ChunkLoadError: Loading chunk 529 failed`** occurs because your browser is attempting to load a stale JavaScript chunk that **no longer exists on the server (HTTP 404)**.

---

### Key Findings & Evidence

#### 1. The Requested Chunk Returns `404 Not Found`
Testing the exact URL from your console:
```bash
curl -I https://qlolabybri.com/widget-chat/_next/static/chunks/__federation_expose_chat_widget.f26aae9f526eead8.js
```
**Response:**
```http
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
X-Powered-By: Next.js
```

#### 2. The Current Server Version Uses a Different Hash
Inspecting the live [`remoteEntry.js`](https://qlolabybri.com/widget-chat/_next/static/chunks/remoteEntry.js) shows that chunk `529` (`__federation_expose_chat_widget`) is mapped to hash **`4bcac9cd9a34cff0`**:
```bash
curl -I https://qlolabybri.com/widget-chat/_next/static/chunks/__federation_expose_chat_widget.4bcac9cd9a34cff0.js
```
**Response:**
```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/javascript; charset=UTF-8
content-length: 174714
last-modified: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 16:36:59 GMT
```

#### 3. Why Did the Browser Request the Old Hash?
This is a classic **Stale Chunk / Deploy Skew** issue caused by caching:

1. **Recent Deployment**:
   A new version was merged and deployed yesterday evening (PR `#95: V1.701.0 release Roxanne` around `Fri Nov 6 17:38 WIB`, container build completed `23:36 WIB`). Webpack generated new chunk hashes (`4bcac9cd9a34cff0`) and pruned the old chunk files (`f26aae9f526eead8`).
2. **`remoteEntry.js` was Cached**:
   `remoteEntry.js` has a 2-hour cache header:
   ```http
   Cache-Control: max-age=7200, public, must-revalidate
   ```
   Because `remoteEntry.js` has **no hash in its filename**, any browser or CDN edge node that visited the site within that window retained the pre-deployment `remoteEntry.js` mapping chunk `529` to `f26aae9f526eead8`.
3. **No Cache Buster in the Host Loader**:
   In [qcash-ui-header-footer `components/contact-support/index.tsx`](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui-header-footer/components/contact-support/index.tsx#L16-L24), the remote is initialized manually without a timestamp query:
   ```ts
   init({
     name: "qcash-ui-live-chat",
     remotes: [
       {
         name: "qcash-ui-live-chat",
         entry: `${config.baseFederation}/widget-chat/_next/static/chunks/remoteEntry.js`, // <-- no ?t= timestamp
       },
     ],
   });
   ```
4. **Offline Flag**:
   When `@module-federation/runtime` fails to fetch the exposed chunk (`chat-widget`), it marks the remote as offline: `qcash-ui-live-chat/chat-widget offline ChunkLoadError`.

---

### Solutions

#### A. Immediate User Fix
- Perform a hard refresh in your browser: **`Ctrl + F5`** (Windows) or **`Cmd + Shift + R`** (Mac), or clear browser cache for `qlolabybri.com`.
- This forces the browser to fetch the updated `remoteEntry.js`, pointing chunk `529` to `4bcac9cd9a34cff0.js`.

---

#### B. Permanent Fixes

##### 1. Disable Cache for `remoteEntry.js` in [next.config.js](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui-livechat/next.config.js)
Files with content hashes (`*.hash.js`) can be cached indefinitely, but entry files without hashes like `remoteEntry.js` should never be cached:

```javascript
// next.config.js in qcash-ui-livechat
const nextConfig = {
  output: "standalone",
  reactStrictMode: true,
  basePath: "/widget-chat",
  async headers() {
    return [
      {
        source: "/:path*/remoteEntry.js",
        headers: [
          {
            key: "Cache-Control",
            value: "no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, proxy-revalidate, max-age=0",
          },
        ],
      },
    ];
  },
  // ... rest of config
};
```

##### 2. Add Timestamp Cache-Busting in [qcash-ui-header-footer](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui-header-footer/components/contact-support/index.tsx#L21)
Ensure host runtime always bypasses stale browser caches:

```typescript
// components/contact-support/index.tsx
init({
  name: "qcash-ui-live-chat",
  remotes: [
    {
      name: "qcash-ui-live-chat",
      entry: `${config.baseFederation}/widget-chat/_next/static/chunks/remoteEntry.js?t=${Date.now()}`,
    },
  ],
});
```

##### 3. Add Retry / Reload Fallback on `ChunkLoadError`
In [contact-support/index.tsx](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui-header-footer/components/contact-support/index.tsx#L31):
```typescript
const ChatWidget: any = dynamic(
  async () => {
    try {
      return await (loadRemote as any)("qcash-ui-live-chat/chat-widget");
    } catch (err: any) {
      if (err?.name === "ChunkLoadError" && typeof window !== "undefined") {
        const hasReloaded = sessionStorage.getItem("chunk_retry_chat");
        if (!hasReloaded) {
          sessionStorage.setItem("chunk_retry_chat", "1");
          window.location.reload();
        }
      }
      throw err;
    }
  },
  { ssr: false }
);
```

## Turn 65: Assistant

You are completely right: **none of the other repos (including `qcash-ui-dashboard`) add a timestamp to their `entry` URL.**

Here is the exact comparison of how **`dashboard`** vs **`live-chat`** is initialized, and why **hard reload did not work**.

---

### 1. Why Hard Reload Is Not Working

When you press `Ctrl + F5` or `Cmd + Shift + R` on `https://qlolabybri.com/v2/landing-page`:

1. The browser bypasses local cache **only for the main HTML document** (`/v2/landing-page`).
2. When the landing page JavaScript runs, Module Federation dynamically injects a `<script>` tag for `remoteEntry.js`:
   ```html
   <script src="https://qlolabybri.com/widget-chat/_next/static/chunks/remoteEntry.js"></script>
   ```
3. Dynamically injected `<script>` tags **do not inherit the document's hard-reload `no-cache` header**.
4. The request hits **Imperva CDN**, which has cached `remoteEntry.js` for 2 hours (`Cache-Control: max-age=7200`):
   ```http
   X-CDN: Imperva
   X-Iinfo: 53-20435082-0 0CNN RT(...)   <-- 0CNN = Imperva Edge Cache HIT (No origin request)
   Last-Modified: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 18:31:40 GMT
   ```
5. Imperva returns the **stale `remoteEntry.js`** from before the deployment, which still asks for chunk `529` as `__federation_expose_chat_widget.f26aae9f526eead8.js`.
6. That chunk file was deleted on the server during the new deployment, returning `404 Not Found`.

---

### 2. Side-by-Side Comparison: `dashboard` vs `live-chat`

Let's look at how [`qcash-ui-dashboard`](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui-dashboard/pages/dashboard/index.tsx) and the shell [`qcash-ui`](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui/constants/features/registry.ts) do `init` vs [`contact-support`](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui-header-footer/components/contact-support/index.tsx).

#### A. Central Registration in Shell (`qcash-ui`)

- **`dashboard`**:
  Registered centrally in [`qcash-ui/constants/features/registry.ts`](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui/constants/features/registry.ts#L64):
  ```typescript
  "qcash-ui-dashboard": {
    name: "qcash-ui-dashboard",
    routes: ["/homepage", "/dashboard"],
    customEntry: remoteEntry("dashboard-v2"), // NO timestamp: /dashboard-v2/_next/static/chunks/remoteEntry.js
  }
  ```
  The shell [`qcash-ui/services/federation/init.ts`](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui/services/federation/init.ts#L48-L68) registers all remotes together in **one** central `init()` with [`RetryPlugin`](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui/services/federation/init.ts#L52):
  ```typescript
  init({
    name: "qcash-ui",
    remotes, // all remotes registered at root shell level
    plugins: [
      RetryPlugin({ script: { retryTimes: 3, retryDelay: 5000 } }),
      fallbackPlugin(),
    ],
  });
  ```

- **`live-chat`**:
  **Completely absent from `qcash-ui`'s `featureRegistry`**. The shell knows nothing about `qcash-ui-live-chat`.

---

#### B. How Standalone / Sub-Repos Call `init()`

Look at how [`qcash-ui-dashboard/pages/dashboard/index.tsx`](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui-dashboard/pages/dashboard/index.tsx#L10-L21) initializes:
```typescript
// qcash-ui-dashboard/pages/dashboard/index.tsx
if (typeof window !== "undefined") {
  init({
    name: "qcash-ui-dashboard", // Host name = ITS OWN NAME
    remotes: [
      {
        name: "qcash-global-component", // Remote name = DEPENDENCY NAME
        entry: `${config.baseFederation}/global-component/_next/static/chunks/remoteEntry.js`,
      },
    ],
  });
  loadRemote("qcash-global-component/globals");
}
```
*Every single other repo in QCash (`qcash-ui-credit-card`, `qcash-ui-registration-online`, `qcash-ui-landing-page`) follows this exact pattern: Host `name` is the container itself, and `remotes` are external dependencies.*

---

#### C. The Bug in [`contact-support/index.tsx`](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui-header-footer/components/contact-support/index.tsx#L14-L27)

Now look at how [`contact-support`](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui-header-footer/components/contact-support/index.tsx#L16-L23) initializes `live-chat`:
```typescript
// qcash-ui-header-footer/components/contact-support/index.tsx
export function initFederation(shouldInit = typeof window !== "undefined") {
  if (shouldInit) {
    init({
      name: "qcash-ui-live-chat", // ❌ BUG: Sets HOST name to the remote's name!
      remotes: [
        {
          name: "qcash-ui-live-chat", // ❌ Remote name is identical to host name!
          entry: `${config.baseFederation}/widget-chat/_next/static/chunks/remoteEntry.js`,
        },
      ],
    });
    loadRemote("qcash-ui-live-chat/globals");
  }
}
```

1. **Host/Remote Collision**:
   Calling `init({ name: "qcash-ui-live-chat", remotes: [{ name: "qcash-ui-live-chat" }] })` inside `qcash-ui-header-footer` creates an instance called `qcash-ui-live-chat` that has itself as a remote.
   When the real `remoteEntry.js` loads, `@module-federation/runtime` warns:
   > *"The remote 'qcash-ui-live-chat' is already registered. OVERRIDE it may have some unexpected errors."*

2. **Calling `init()` instead of `registerRemotes()`**:
   In `@module-federation/runtime`, once an app (like `qcash-ui` or `landing-page`) is already running, **you must not call `init()` again** in a sub-component.
   The correct API to register an additional remote dynamically is **[`registerRemotes`](https://module-federation.io/guide/basic/runtime.html)**.

---

#### D. Missing Singletons in [`qcash-ui-livechat/next.config.js`](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui-livechat/next.config.js#L19-L36)

- In [`qcash-ui-dashboard/next.config.js`](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui-dashboard/next.config.js#L55-L57):
  ```javascript
  shared: {
    react: { singleton: true, requiredVersion: false },
    "react-dom": { singleton: true, requiredVersion: false },
    next: { singleton: true, requiredVersion: false },
    // ...
  }
  ```
- In [`qcash-ui-livechat/next.config.js`](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui-livechat/next.config.js#L19-L36):
  `react`, `react-dom`, and `next` are **not listed in `shared` at all**.
  Because they are omitted, Webpack compiles internal exposes (`__federation_expose_react_dom`, `__federation_expose_react`) that depend on individual chunk hashes (like chunk `529`).

---

### 3. Summary of Differences

| Aspect | `qcash-ui-dashboard` | `qcash-ui-livechat` (`contact-support`) |
|---|---|---|
| **Timestamp in entry URL** | ❌ None | ❌ None |
| **Shell registry** | ✅ Registered centrally in `qcash-ui`'s `featureRegistry` | ❌ Not in `featureRegistry`; dynamically pulled by `contact-support` |
| **Federation Host Name** | `name: "qcash-ui-dashboard"` (Clean) | `name: "qcash-ui-live-chat"` (Collides with remote name) |

## Turn 102: Assistant

That conditional check was an **unnecessary defensive branch** (overengineering). 

### Why It Was There
I initially added that `if/else` check because `@module-federation/runtime` has two different methods:
- `registerRemotes()`: used to append a remote to an existing host instance.
- `init()`: used when no instance exists yet.

However, in Module Federation, **`init()` already supports multiple independent named instances** without needing `registerRemotes()`.

### The Actual 1-Line Fix
In [`qcash-ui-dashboard`](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui-dashboard/pages/dashboard/index.tsx#L12), notice how it simply calls `init()`:
```typescript
init({
  name: "qcash-ui-dashboard", // Host name = this repo
  remotes: [{ name: "qcash-global-component", entry: "..." }],
});
```

The only bug in [`contact-support/index.tsx`](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui-header-footer/components/contact-support/index.tsx#L17) was a copy-paste/typo: **the author set the host `name` to `"qcash-ui-live-chat"` instead of `"qcash-ui-header-footer"`**:
```diff
 export function initFederation(shouldInit = typeof window !== "undefined") {
   if (shouldInit) {
     init({
-      name: "qcash-ui-live-chat",
+      name: "qcash-ui-header-footer",
       remotes: [
         {
           name: "qcash-ui-live-chat",
           entry: `${config.baseFederation}/widget-chat/_next/static/chunks/remoteEntry.js`,
         },
       ],
     });
     loadRemote("qcash-ui-live-chat/globals");
   }
 }
```

### Cleaned Up
I have removed the conditional branch. The diff in [`qcash-ui-header-footer`](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui-header-footer/components/contact-support/index.tsx) is now just that **single line**: setting `name: "qcash-ui-header-footer"` so it cleanly matches how `dashboard` and every other repo in QCash operates.

## Turn 104: Assistant

In Module Federation, `name` and `remotes` have two very different meanings:

```typescript
init({
  name: "WHO_I_AM",      // The Host/Consumer container running this code
  remotes: [
    {
      name: "WHAT_I_LOAD", // The Remote module being imported
      entry: "URL_TO_REMOTE_ENTRY",
    },
  ],
});
```

### Why `name` must be `qcash-ui-header-footer`, NOT `qcash-ui-live-chat`

1. **`contact-support` lives inside `qcash-ui-header-footer`**:
   The code running in this file is the **consumer**. Its container name is `"qcash-ui-header-footer"`.

2. **`live-chat` is what is being loaded**:
   `live-chat` belongs in the **`remotes`** array:
   ```typescript
   remotes: [
     {
       name: "qcash-ui-live-chat", // <-- Live chat is already specified HERE
       entry: `${config.baseFederation}/widget-chat/_next/static/chunks/remoteEntry.js`,
     },
   ]
   ```

3. **What happens if you put `name: "qcash-ui-live-chat"` at the top level?**
   - You are telling Module Federation: *"I am the live-chat container."*
   - And then you also say: *"I want to load live-chat as my remote."*
   - When the actual `remoteEntry.js` from `live-chat` finishes downloading and executes, it tries to register itself with `name: "qcash-ui-live-chat"`.
   - Module Federation's runtime detects that an instance named `"qcash-ui-live-chat"` already exists (the consumer you created) and throws:
     > `The remote "qcash-ui-live-chat" is already registered. OVERRIDE it may have some unexpected errors.`
   - In short, **the caller and the callee have the exact same name**, causing Module Federation to confuse who is the host and who is the remote.

---

### Compare with other repos in QCash

Notice how every other repo in the codebase does this:

| File | Who is loading it (`name`) | What it is loading (`remotes[0].name`) |
|---|---|---|
| **`landing-page`** (`components/contact-menu/index.tsx`) | `name: "qcash-ui-landing-page"` | `remotes: [{ name: "qcash-ui-header-footer" }]` |
| **`dashboard`** (`pages/dashboard/index.tsx`) | `name: "qcash-ui-dashboard"` | `remotes: [{ name: "qcash-global-component" }]` |
| **`credit-card`** (`components/create-modal/index.tsx`) | `name: "qcash-ui-credit-card"` | `remotes: [{ name: "qcash-global-component" }]` |
| **`contact-support`** (`components/contact-support/index.tsx`) | **`name: "qcash-ui-header-footer"`** | **`remotes: [{ name: "qcash-ui-live-chat" }]`** |

`live-chat` is already listed as the target in `remotes[0].name`. The top-level `name` is the identity of the host (`qcash-ui-header-footer`).

## Turn 118: Assistant

This screenshot reveals the exact mechanism of the intermittent failure:

---

### 1. Why `Refused to execute script ... MIME type ('text/html')` Appears

When Webpack requests chunk `255.0cbc767518c4d.js` from the server:
```bash
curl -I https://qlolabybri.com/widget-chat/_next/static/chunks/255.0cbc767518c4d.js
```
The server responds with:
```http
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8   <--- Next.js 404 HTML page!
X-Powered-By: Next.js
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
```
Because the file was deleted in the new deployment, Next.js falls back to its default **404 HTML page**. When the browser tries to parse that HTML error page as JavaScript, Chrome/Edge blocks it:
> *"Refused to execute script ... because its MIME type ('text/html') is not executable, and strict MIME type checking is enabled."*

Immediately after that, Webpack rejects the chunk load promise:
> *"ChunkLoadError: Loading chunk 529 failed."*

---

### 2. Why Does It Work "Sometimes"?

There are two reasons this flaps between working and failing:

#### Reason A: Browser Cache Desynchronization (Most Common)
* **When it FAILS**:
  Your browser still has the pre-deployment `remoteEntry.js` in memory/disk cache (because of `Cache-Control: max-age=7200` = 2 hours). That old entry file maps chunks to:
  - `Chunk 255` ➔ `255.0cbc767518c4d...` *(no longer on server)*
  - `Chunk 529` ➔ `__federation_expose_chat_widget.f26aae9f526eead8.js` *(no longer on server)*
  When Webpack tries to download them, the server returns 404 HTML.

* **When it SUCCEEDS**:
  If you open an **Incognito tab**, clear browser cache, or open the page after the 2-hour cache TTL expires:
  - The browser fetches the **new** `remoteEntry.js`.
  - The new `remoteEntry.js` requests the **new** chunk hash:
    `__federation_expose_chat_widget.4bcac9cd9a34cff0.js`
  - That chunk exists on the server (`HTTP 200 OK`, 174 KB), and the chat loads without any error.

---

#### Reason B: OpenShift Multi-Pod / Ingress Skew (During Deployments)
In OpenShift/Kubernetes, requests pass through Imperva and OpenShift HAProxy routers:
- If a rolling deployment is in progress (or if an old pod/replica is still terminating/responding):
  1. Request 1 (`remoteEntry.js`) hits **Pod A** (old build): returns old manifest pointing to `f26aae9f526eead8.js`.
  2. Request 2 (`f26aae9f526eead8.js`) hits **Pod B** (new build): Pod B does not have that old file and returns 404 HTML.
- In Imperva, notice the `nlbi_3320853` cookie in your network request: Imperva uses this for backend load balancer affinity. Switching sessions or IP routes can hit different pods or edge caches.

---

### How Our Code Fix Prevents This Permanently

1. **`remoteEntry.js` No-Cache Header** (in [`qcash-ui-livechat/next.config.js`](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui-livechat/next.config.js#L44-L56)):
   Forces `remoteEntry.js` to always be fetched with `no-store, no-cache, max-age=0`. The browser will **never** hold onto an outdated manifest pointing to deleted chunk hashes.

2. **Fixed Host Name** (in [`qcash-ui-header-footer/components/contact-support/index.tsx`](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui-header-footer/components/contact-support/index.tsx#L17)):
   Setting `name: "qcash-ui-header-footer"` prevents the host container from colliding with and hijacking the `qcash-ui-live-chat` instance.

## Turn 130: Assistant

The timestamp injection (`?t=...`) is handled automatically by **`@module-federation/nextjs-mf`** in its internal runtime plugin.

Here are the exact files and lines of code responsible:

---

### 1. The Primary Injector (In-Browser Runtime)
📁 [`node_modules/@module-federation/nextjs-mf/dist/src/plugins/container/runtimePlugin.js`](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui/node_modules/@module-federation/nextjs-mf/dist/src/plugins/container/runtimePlugin.js#L59-L72) **(Lines 59–72)**

Whenever `FederationHost.loadRemote()` is called, `@module-federation/nextjs-mf` intercepts the request via its `beforeRequest` lifecycle hook and injects `?t=${Date.now()}`:

```javascript
// runtimePlugin.js (Lines 59-72)
beforeRequest: (args) => {
    const { options, id } = args;
    const remoteName = id.split('/').shift();
    const remote = options.remotes.find((remote) => remote.name === remoteName);
    if (!remote)
        return args;
    //@ts-ignore
    if (remote?.entry?.includes('?t=')) {
        return args;
    }
    //@ts-ignore
    remote.entry = `${remote?.entry}?t=${Date.now()}`; // <-- LINE 70: Injects the timestamp
    return args;
},
```

---

### 2. SSR Chunk Injection (Server-Side Rendering)
📁 [`node_modules/@module-federation/nextjs-mf/dist/utils/flushedChunks.js`](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui/node_modules/@module-federation/nextjs-mf/dist/utils/flushedChunks.js#L46-L48) **(Lines 46–48)**

When Next.js flushes initial remote script tags to the document:

```javascript
// flushedChunks.js (Lines 46-48)
if (!chunk.includes('?') && chunk.includes('remoteEntry')) {
    chunk = chunk + '?t=' + Date.now(); // <-- LINE 47: Injects timestamp into flushed script tag
}
```

---

### 3. Application Plugin That Strips It
📁 [`qcash-ui/services/federation/init.ts`](file:///C:/Work/qcash-ui/services/federation/init.ts#L17-L29) **(Lines 17–29)**

In your main shell container, notice there is a plugin specifically written to remove that injected timestamp for certain remotes (like `qui`):

```typescript
// qcash-ui/services/federation/init.ts (Lines 17-29)
const stripTimestampPlugin = () => ({
  name: "strip-timestamp-plugin",
  beforeRequest(args: any) {
    const { options, id } = args;
    const remoteName = id.split("/").shift();
    const remote = options.remotes.find((r: any) => r.name === remoteName);

    if (remote && ETAG_CACHED_REMOTES.has(remote.name)) {
      remote.entry = remote.entry.replace(/\?t=\d+$/, ""); // <-- LINE 25: Strips the injected timestamp
    }

    return args;
  },
});
```

---

### Summary
* When a remote is loaded via `@module-federation/nextjs-mf`'s built-in container runtime, **`runtimePlugin.js:70`** automatically appends `?t=${Date.now()}`.
* When remotes are manually registered via custom `@module-federation/runtime` calls (like in `contact-support`), that automatic `runtimePlugin` is bypassed unless explicitly added or configured.

---
